about: Six defects seeded into the kit's own statutory_deadline (shared/desk_calc.py), one each (workshop lesson 10.10). Each is a one-line substitution on the function as the kit holds it: old must occur exactly once, or commands/ralph.py stops and says the seed needs refreshing. rule is the defect's class in commands/review_diff.py's rubric; weak and strong are the oracle's verdicts, which make ralph-check and commands/tests/test_ralph.py hold. why is for people: the reviewer never sees it.

seeds.name: placeholder
seeds.why: The date the selftest's one case expects, hard-coded: desk_calc's own selftest passes it, and only the sweep over every day of 2026 catches it.

seeds.name: calendar_days
seeds.why: Two calendar days, not two working days: a Thursday or a Friday gives a Saturday or a Sunday.

seeds.name: start_day_counted
seeds.why: The last working day counted as the first of the two, so the wages fall due a working day early.

seeds.name: closure_counted
seeds.why: s.17(2) names the closure of the establishment, but counts the two days from a removal, dismissal, retrenchment or resignation only: the desk refuses closure, and this accepts it.

seeds.name: date_contract
seeds.why: day_of() re-written by hand: a date not written YYYY-MM-DD now raises Python's ValueError, which the Desk's tool does not turn into an error result (desk_agent._calc catches CalcError), so the person's turn fails instead of the model reading the refusal. The selftest never sends a bad date.

seeds.name: holiday_note_dropped
seeds.old: notes=[NO_HOLIDAYS, "Counted from the last working day
seeds.new: notes=["Counted from the last working day
seeds.why: The date assumes no holiday falls in between (no holiday calendar is loaded), and the result no longer says so.
